newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Telecom nearly halfway through shr buyback.
newsitem.headline: Telecom nearly halfway through shr buyback.

text.p: Telecom Corp of New Zealand said on Tuesday it had achieved nearly 44 percent of its NZ$1 billion share buyback target.
It said that during February and March, in the first of its four planned purchase periods, more than one third of the repurchases had been completed.

Telecom aims to buy NZ$1 billion of shares in the current year. It has identified four major periods, after each quarterly profit announcement, in which it is purchasing shares on-market, and from major shareholders Ameritech and Bell Atlantic off-market.
The latest purchases from those companies were made on Monday at NZ$6.86 when the company bought 105,476 shares, Telecom said in a separate statement.
Telecom also said it had set up the following procedural safeguards designed to ensure that its buyback programme does not create market distortions -
* purchasing through only one broker on any single day,
* not taking part in the opening transaction on during the final specified period of trading each day,
* not purchasing at a price which exceeds the higher current independent published bid or the last independent sale price (whichever is higher),
* not exceeding restrictions on volume of trading in proportion to the total trading volume,
* purchasing shares during the periods of approximately six weeks immediately following the announcements of Telecom's quarterly results,
* notifying daily the details of on-market purchases (i.e. the quantity purchased and price paid).
Telecom said it had purchased just 105,000 of the 1.6 million Telecom shares traded on Thursday, with all shares bought at below the average price of $6.90.
On Friday last week, Telecom purchased a similar percentage of its total shares traded, the company said.
"This clearly illustrates investors are purchasing shares at prices that are in excess of what Telecom is paying," it said.
